title: A boundary-only obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding
coverage: I read every section in full (introduction, geometry, deformation, connections, algebra, frobenius, conclusion) and traced the chain of implications. Geometry: the graph homotopy type of G and the peripheral data (Lemma geo:graph); the capped-stage construction; the dual-sphere invariants, including the label-cancellation argument through the unused y-cap complex K, which has trivial pi_1; and the reduction from embedded discs to cut data (Lemma geo:topological-cuts, which uses an ANR extension). It uses only that the discs are embedded and pairwise disjoint, not that they are locally flat. Deformation: the two-sheeted-cover Mayer-Vietoris maps, half-lives-half-dies (Lagrangian) slopes and complementary tangents, the equation-chart small-extension argument, and cubic nilpotence via Nakayama. I checked numerically that Ad rho(c) for reduced words of length at most 5 spans End(sl2): rank 9, already at length 4. I also checked [E,[H,F]] = -2H. Connections: I re-derived the sign of the polarized Chern-Simons variation formula; checked the derivative-ideal proof (curvature class killed on both wall copies by Poincare-Lefschetz pairing, then degree-two Mayer-Vietoris injectivity, then a flat lift contradicting the chart lemma); and checked the value identity (collar modification, exactly flat connection on Q over the free group, gauge versus connection comparison, Stokes). Algebra: the ninth-order replacement estimates, the Nakayama preservation of (v)=r, the graph correction Y+Bv, witness transport, and specialization. Frobenius: socle/residue nonvanishing, Res(d omega)=0, Kunneth and tensor-kernel lemma, the retraction homotopy, the cycle lift over k[s]/(s^2), the moving normal form, and the final w*b_s=0 contradiction. In the p_i=0 case the Frobenius argument reduces to a simple pairing argument, and that is consistent with small hand examples I tried. I could not build counterexample data. Less deeply checked: the Zariski-Nagata/primary-decomposition step in Lemma alg:replacement, the finite-sum jet control in Prop conn:all-jets, and the ribbon/framing details in Lemma geo:framing and geo:stages.
main_claim: Theorem 1.1: there is a compact oriented smooth 4-manifold M with finitely many proper immersed discs f_i (disjoint embedded boundaries) and framed embedded spheres g_i with lambda(f_i,g_j)=delta_ij, lambda(g_i,g_j)=0 and mu~(g_i)=0, such that the boundary circles bound no pairwise disjoint locally flat embedded discs. Consequences: F_2 is not good, and the unrestricted surgery and s-cobordism conjectures cannot both hold. Proof route: hypothetical discs give cuts of a graph-homotopy-equivalent G along walls with one torus boundary each, and the triple-commutator relations hold in the cut piece X_Q. SL2 deformations then give a cube-zero end-holonomy ideal and polarized Chern-Simons wall potentials with (dPsi)=r and Psi in r^2. Algebraic replacement and specialization to characteristic l follow, and a Frobenius-Koszul residue argument gives the contradiction for d>=5.
sibling_notes: There were no prior sibling entries for family 305. I posted a no_gap_found summary to the board. The claim is extraordinary (it would settle the open free-group goodness problem), so although I found no failing step, the wall-potential identities in Secs 3-4 and the replacement lemma deserve independent expert scrutiny.
